title: Completion of a polynomial nodal model at the origin
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $h\in\mathfrak m$. Set $k=A/\mathfrak m$, $P=A[x,y]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mP+(x,y)$, $D=P_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $R=A[[x,y]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak mR+(x,y)$. Then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, and the polynomial-to-series map induces $A$-algebra isomorphisms $P/\mathfrak q^r\xrightarrow{\sim}D/(\mathfrak qD)^r\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak a^r$ for every $r\ge1$, compatible with transition maps and preserving constants and variables. It induces $\widehat D\cong R$ as $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $M_h=\operatorname{Spec}(P/(xy-h))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $o\in M_h$ be the point with ideal $\mathfrak q/(xy-h)$. Then $\mathcal O_{M_h,o}\cong D/(xy-h)D$ as $A$-algebras, $\kappa(o)\cong k$ through the coefficient map [def-weil-residue-field], and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{M_h,o}\cong R/(xy-h)$ as $A$-algebras preserving constants and the classes of $x,y$. All completions are at the respective maximal ideals.

proof.text: Constant-term evaluation followed by $A\to k$ gives a surjection $P\to k$ whose kernel is $\mathfrak q$: a polynomial minus its constant term lies in $(x,y)$, and its constant term maps to zero precisely when it lies in $\mathfrak m$. Thus $P/\mathfrak q=k$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $D$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qD$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, third paragraph: the origin of the polynomial model; explicit evaluation calculation.

proof.text: For $r\ge1$ and $p=\sum_E c_Ex^E\in P$, expansion of the ideal power gives $\mathfrak q^r=\sum_{j=0}^r\mathfrak m^{r-j}P\,(x,y)^j$. Hence membership implies $c_E\in\mathfrak m^{r-|E|}$ whenever $|E|<r$: every degree-$|E|$ contribution from the $j$th summand has $j\le |E|$ and coefficient in $\mathfrak m^{r-j}\subseteq\mathfrak m^{r-|E|}$. Conversely, if these coefficient conditions hold, each low-degree term is in $\mathfrak m^{r-|E|}P\,(x,y)^{|E|}\subseteq\mathfrak q^r$, and each of the finitely many remaining monomials has degree at least $r$ and belongs to $(x,y)^r$. Adding these terms proves the converse.

source.place: Elementary expansion of the combined ideal power, using the finite-monomial definition of a polynomial; supplies the finite-quotient identification implicit in curves Tag 0CBY.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $\Lambda=A$, $J=\mathfrak m$, $d=2$, $n=r$. The criterion of Step 2 is therefore equivalent to the image of $p$ lying in $\mathfrak a^r$. Thus $P/\mathfrak q^r\to R/\mathfrak a^r$ is injective. It is surjective: for $F=\sum_E c_Ex^E$, the finite polynomial $p_{<r}=\sum_{|E|<r}c_Ex^E$ has $F-p_{<r}\in\mathfrak a^r$, by that same cited criterion since all its coefficients below degree $r$ vanish. Consequently the polynomial inclusion gives an $A$-algebra isomorphism $u_r:P/\mathfrak q^r\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak a^r$.

proof.text: If $s\in P\setminus\mathfrak q$, write $s=c+t$ with $c\in A\setminus\mathfrak m$ a unit and $t\in(x,y)$. In $P/\mathfrak q^r$ its inverse is $c^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(-t/c)^j$, since the error is a multiple of $t^r\in\mathfrak q^r$. Thus $P\to P/\mathfrak q^r$ extends to $D\to P/\mathfrak q^r$, by $p/s\mapsto\bar p\bar s^{-1}$; the fraction relations show this is well defined. It kills $(\mathfrak qD)^r=\mathfrak q^rD$. The induced map $D/(\mathfrak qD)^r\to P/\mathfrak q^r$ is inverse to the natural map $v_r$ in the other direction: the composites fix $\bar p$ and the fractions $\overline{p/s}$, respectively. This proves the first required isomorphism.

source.place: Definition Tag 00CO, definition-localization; elementary geometric-sum inverse in the nilpotent quotient. No localization-commutes-with-quotient theorem is needed here.

proof.text: The inclusion $P\to R$ also extends to an $A$-algebra map $j:D\to R$. Indeed, for $s=c+t$ as in Step 4, put $w=t/c$. The formal series $c^{-1}\sum_{j\ge0}(-w)^j$ is well defined: the coefficient at degree $e$ involves only $j\le e$, because $w$ has zero constant term. Multiplying by $s=c(1+w)$ cancels consecutive terms and gives $1$ in each coefficient. The usual fraction formula therefore defines $j(p/s)=p\,j(s)^{-1}$. It sends $\mathfrak qD$ into $\mathfrak a$ and induces $w_r:D/(\mathfrak qD)^r\to R/\mathfrak a^r$ with $w_rv_r=u_r$; hence $w_r=u_rv_r^{-1}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Definition Tag 00CO, definition-localization, and the coefficientwise power-series definition; elementary formal geometric-sum calculation underlying the map of curves Tag 0CBY.

proof.text: For $r\ge s\ge1$, the reduction of each map $u_r,v_r,w_r$ equals the corresponding map at level $s$: both composites on a polynomial class send $p$ to its same class at level $s$, and on a localized class they send $p/t$ to the class of $p$ times the inverse of the class of $t$. This checks every transition square, rather than choosing abstract quotient isomorphisms. Each map fixes the image of every $a\in A$ and sends $x,y$ to their named images, by its construction from the inclusion and the fraction formula.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, third paragraph; explicit naturality of the polynomial model comparison.

proof.text: The compatible family $w_r$ gives $\widehat D\cong\varprojlim_r R/\mathfrak a^r$ by [lem-trf-adic-inverse-limit-iso]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] with $\Lambda=A$, $J=\mathfrak m$, $d=2$: its hypotheses are exactly Noetherianity and the assumed $\mathfrak m$-adic completeness of $A$. By [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_rR/\mathfrak a^r$ is an isomorphism. Compose its inverse to obtain $e:\widehat D\xrightarrow{\sim}R$. Its projection at every $r$ is $w_r$, so $e(c_D(d))=j(d)$ for all $d\in D$, where $c_D$ is the completion map: their images in every $R/\mathfrak a^r$ coincide and completeness includes separatedness. In particular $e$ is an $A$-algebra isomorphism and preserves $x,y$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, third paragraph; expand the implicit polynomial-to-complete-local identification via coefficient completeness (Algebra Tag 032C).

proof.text: Put $f=xy-h$. Since $h\in\mathfrak m$, $f\in\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q/(f)$ is a maximal ideal of $P/(f)$ with quotient $k$ by Step 1. Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] on the whole affine scheme $M_h$ and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] with ring $P$, ideal $(f)$ and prime $\mathfrak q/(f)$. These give $B:=\mathcal O_{M_h,o}\cong(P/(f))_{\mathfrak q/(f)}\cong D/fD$. The maps send fractions to fractions, so preserve $A$ and $x,y$. This quotient is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=(\mathfrak qD)/fD$: an element outside that ideal lifts outside the maximal ideal of $D$ and is a unit. By Step 4 at $r=1$, $B/\mathfrak n=D/\mathfrak qD\cong P/\mathfrak q=k$ through the coefficient map, which is $\kappa(o)\cong k$ by [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, third paragraph; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6); Algebra Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient.

proof.text: The ring $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since $P=A[x,y]/(0)$, and $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] with multiplicative set $P\setminus\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] to the surjection $\lambda:D\to B\cong D/fD$, whose kernel is $fD$ and whose image of the maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n$ of Step 8. It yields the canonical isomorphism $\widehat D/f\widehat D\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat B$, induced by the quotient maps at every level. Under $e$ of Step 7 the element $c_D(f)$ is $xy-h$, so $e$ carries $f\widehat D$ exactly onto $(xy-h)R$. Inverting the preceding quotient-completion isomorphism and then applying $e$ on quotients gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{M_h,o}\cong R/(xy-h)$. The cited completion-quotient theorem satisfies $\theta c_D=c_B\lambda$; together with $e c_D=j$, this shows that the last isomorphism sends $c_B(\lambda(a))$ to $a\bmod(xy-h)$ for every $a\in A$ and sends $c_B(\lambda(x)),c_B(\lambda(y))$ to the classes of $x,y$. It is therefore the required $A$-algebra isomorphism. Its completions are precisely at $\mathfrak qD$ and $\mathfrak n$, the respective maximal ideals.
